explanation: The theorem is the limiting case p = n of the Sobolev inequality, with an explicit constant: for any q ≥ n it bounds ‖u‖_q by μ(Ω)^{1/q} times ‖Du‖_n. The proof uses only the library's own `eLpNorm_le_mul_measure_rpow_mul_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_lt` (TauCeti/Analysis/Sobolev/FiniteMeasure.lean), which is not in Mathlib, plus some algebra on the exponents. Mathlib's Sobolev inequalities are in Mathlib/Analysis/FunctionalSpaces/SobolevInequality.lean. I read all of them: `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_one`, `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_eq_inner`, `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_eq`, `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_le` and `eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv`. They cover only p = 1 or p < finrank, they use constants that are not explicit, and most of them need F to be finite-dimensional or an inner product space. None treats p = finrank E or has this constant in terms of μ(Ω).
